G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
REGIONAL HEAD
Raghav Khanna
Training Framework  ·  7–14 days at Chandigarh HQ
Structured around the customer journey, not the org chart

How This Training Works
Every Regional Head goes through this program at Chandigarh HQ before being deployed. The program runs 7 to 14 days. Length depends on the trainee's learning curve. Sign-off comes from every trainer, not from time spent.

Two streams, in sequence
The training follows the customer's journey through GLEUHR, not the org chart.

STREAM 1 — SALES (end-to-end). Lead generation → online appointments team → branch coordination → counsellor closing → follow-ups, upsell, cross-sell. Owned by Manisha (Head of Sales).
STREAM 2 — OPERATIONS (clinic floor). Reception → doctors & clinical → therapists → housekeeping & hygiene → compliance. Owned by Saurabh (Operations Manager).

Why this sequence.  The Regional Head must understand how a person becomes a paying customer before they understand how a clinic operates. Revenue lives in sales; brand lives in operations. The trainee experiences both in the order a customer experiences them — call first, walk in second, treatment third. By Day 7 to 14, the trainee can trace any revenue or quality issue back to where in the journey it began.

Sign-off principle
Sign-off requires evidence of competence, not attendance.  Every trainer must confirm the trainee can independently run that module's standard before they sign. A trainer who signs without confidence is doing the company harm — quietly. Manisha and Saurabh review every sign-off before the trainee is deployed.

STREAM 1  ·  SALES — End to End
This stream takes the trainee from the moment a lead is generated to the moment a customer renews or upgrades. Manisha owns this stream. Her team — the online appointments team lead, the senior counsellor at Chandigarh, and the marketing function — deliver the modules.

Modules in this stream
Module 1 — Online Appointments Team (lead handoff, scheduling, no-show, branch coordination)
Module 2 — Branch Sales Coordination (handoff from online team to branch reception)
Module 3 — Counsellor Closing (consultation, package conversion, objection handling)
Module 4 — Follow-ups, Upsell, Cross-sell (post-purchase, retention, renewal)

Module 1  ·  Online Appointments Team
First module. The Regional Head must understand how a lead becomes a booked appointment, before they understand anything else. This is the funnel's first conversion event.

Context the trainee needs to know
Aspect
Current state
Team size
40 to 45 callers
No-show rate (booked clients who don't arrive)
40 to 50%
Standardised call flow
Not in place — being developed
Follow-ups and automations
Weak — needs rebuilding
Lead nurturing
Currently being developed

The honest framing.  The Regional Head should know — on Day 1 of this module — that this part of the business is being rebuilt, not running well. The 40-50% no-show rate is what we are working to reduce. The trainee is not being trained to admire the current state; they are being trained to understand where the gaps are so they can support fixes at branch level.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Explain how a lead flows through the online appointments team — from first call to confirmed booking
Understand what a good call flow looks like and identify gaps in the current one
Understand the handoff from online team to branch reception — what information transfers, what gets lost
Recognise the patterns behind the 40-50% no-show rate and identify branch-side factors the Regional Head can influence
Know what follow-up and nurturing should look like when the new automation is in place
Recognise when a branch-level issue (poor reception experience, long wait times, weak first impressions) is contributing to no-shows

Training activities
Day 1: Sit with the online appointments team for half a day. Observe live calls. Listen to call recordings.
Day 1: Walk through the lead-to-booking funnel with the team lead. Understand each stage's drop-off.
Day 2: Review the last 30 days of no-show data — by branch, by day-of-week, by lead source. Identify patterns.
Day 2: Sit with Manisha for 60 minutes. Discuss what the online team is being rebuilt to look like.
Day 2: Map the handoff from online team to a real branch. What information moves? What is lost?

Sign-off criteria
Can explain the current state of the online appointments team clearly and honestly
Has reviewed no-show patterns and articulated three branch-side factors that contribute
Manisha confirms readiness in writing

Module 2  ·  Branch Sales Coordination
Once a client is booked, what happens? This module covers the handoff from the online appointments team to the branch, the role of reception in confirming the booking, and how the BM and counsellor team prepare for the day's bookings.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Trace a booked appointment from the online team's CRM entry to the moment the client walks into the branch
Identify where information is lost in the handoff
Understand the reception's role in confirmation calls, day-before reminders, and arrival prep
Recognise when the BM is preparing the day's bookings well versus when bookings are walking in cold

Training activities
Day 1: Trace 10 bookings end-to-end at Chandigarh — from online team CRM to branch arrival
Day 1: Observe the reception's confirmation call process. Audit a day's confirmation calls.
Day 2: Sit with Jaspreet (BM) for the morning huddle — see how the day's bookings are prepared

Sign-off criteria
Can describe the full handoff in writing
Has identified the three biggest gaps in the current handoff
Manisha + Jaspreet confirm readiness

Module 3  ·  Counsellor Closing
Where revenue is actually generated. The counsellor consultation, the conversion into package, objection handling, package design.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Observe a counselling session and identify the three things being done well and the three being done poorly
Audit a CRM record and identify inflated promises, missing follow-ups, or incomplete documentation
Coach a counsellor on objection-handling and honest expectations
Understand the four core sales KPIs — conversion into package, total revenue, overall conversion rate, upsell/cross-sell — and what good looks like for each
Run the counsellor scorecard end-to-end

Training activities
Day 1: Sit in on 3 counsellor consultations as observer
Day 2: Review yesterday's counsellor CRM records with Senior Counsellor
Day 2: Live coaching exercise — sit in on a session, then debrief
Day 3: Telephony audit — pull a day's call data, identify real follow-ups vs dialled-and-dropped
Day 3: Worried-about-clients exercise — go through Chandigarh's list

Sign-off criteria
Can identify counselling-quality issues in a live session
Can audit CRM records independently
Has run at least 2 coaching conversations with counsellors
Can explain the four core sales KPIs and what affects each
Senior Counsellor + Manisha confirm readiness

Module 4  ·  Follow-ups, Upsell, Cross-sell
After the package is purchased, the relationship begins — or ends. This module is about what happens between the first purchase and the next one.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Understand the post-purchase journey — what the client experiences between treatments and after package completion
Identify upsell opportunities (adding a service to existing package) and cross-sell opportunities (new category)
Read the renewal rate and explain what drives a customer to renew vs lapse
Coach a counsellor on running honest upsell conversations — the ones that don't damage trust
Identify lapsed-client win-back opportunities and the right way to approach them

Training activities
Day 1: Review 30 days of upsell/cross-sell records at Chandigarh
Day 1: Sit with Senior Counsellor on a post-treatment client meeting
Day 2: Lapsed-clients exercise — pull the list, build a re-engagement plan for 5
Day 2: Sit with Manisha for 60 minutes on the four core sales KPIs — how to track, how to improve

Sign-off criteria
Can articulate the post-purchase journey end-to-end
Can read renewal and retention data and explain what is driving the numbers
Has built a re-engagement plan for at least 5 lapsed clients
Manisha confirms readiness in writing

STREAM 2  ·  OPERATIONS — Clinic Floor
This stream covers everything that happens once a client is inside the four walls of a branch. Saurabh owns this stream. His team — the senior doctor at Chandigarh, the senior therapist, Arshpreet for compliance, and Jaspreet for reception — deliver the modules.

Modules in this stream
Module 5 — Reception (in-clinic operations of greeting, hospitality, CRM)
Module 6 — Doctors & Clinical Protocols
Module 7 — Therapists & Treatment Delivery
Module 8 — Housekeeping, Hygiene & Compliance

Module 5  ·  Reception (In-Clinic)
Once the client walks in, the front desk is the brand. Different scope from Module 2 (which covered the handoff and confirmation calls). This module is about what happens face-to-face at the desk.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Walk into any branch's reception and audit it against the GLEUHR standard within 15 minutes
Identify gaps in greeting, CRM use, water/tea hospitality, appointment management, and phone handling
Coach a struggling receptionist on the same day, in a 10-minute conversation
Run the reception scorecard end-to-end

Training activities
Day 1: Shadow reception at Chandigarh for one full shift
Day 2: Co-run reception alongside Jaspreet
Day 2: Independent reception verification walk + sign-off

Sign-off criteria
Can score the reception team accurately using the 10-item scorecard
Has successfully coached at least one reception team member
Jaspreet + Saurabh confirm readiness

Module 6  ·  Doctors & Clinical Protocols
Critical caution.  The Regional Head is NOT a clinical authority. They cannot diagnose, override clinical decisions, or interfere with treatment plans. This module is about understanding the clinical work well enough to support it operationally — not to direct it.

What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Understand the key treatments offered at GLEUHR, what each is for, typical outcomes, and realistic timelines
Recognise clinical hygiene gaps, machine cleanliness issues, and protocol breaches
Know when something is a clinical decision (escalate) vs an operational issue
Hold doctors accountable for non-clinical standards — punctuality, communication, CRM documentation

Training activities
Day 1: Walk through every treatment cabin with Senior Doctor
Day 1: Sit in on 2-3 doctor consultations
Day 2: Review treatment protocols document
Day 2: Hygiene audit exercise with Arshpreet
Day 2: Boundary exercise — 10 'clinical vs operational' scenarios

Sign-off criteria
Can explain every treatment in plain terms
Can identify hygiene and protocol gaps independently
Demonstrates clear understanding of clinical vs operational boundaries
Senior Doctor + Saurabh confirm readiness

Module 7  ·  Therapists & Treatment Delivery
What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Audit a therapist's treatment delivery — cabin prep, machine handling, communication, post-treatment cleaning
Identify therapists who are rushing sessions, skipping protocols, or providing inconsistent client experience
Coach a therapist on technique and bedside manner
Spot training gaps in therapist workforce

Training activities
Day 1: Shadow 2 different therapists through full client sessions
Day 2: Review therapist workload and scheduling
Day 2: Live audit + coaching exercise

Sign-off criteria
Can audit treatment delivery independently
Has coached at least one therapist successfully
Senior Therapist + Saurabh confirm readiness

Module 8  ·  Housekeeping, Hygiene & Compliance
What the Regional Head must be able to do by end of module
Audit housekeeping work end-to-end — floor, dusting, deep cleaning, washroom, machine cleaning, refreshments
Communicate with low-literacy housekeeping staff in their language and register
Coach the housekeeping team without triggering withdrawal or fear
Run hygiene audits at the level of the founder's expectation
Understand the compliance audit framework Saurabh uses across all branches

Training activities
Day 1: Walk with Arshpreet through her full daily hygiene audit
Day 2: Independent audit attempt vs Arshpreet's
Day 2: Observe Arshpreet's housekeeping debrief in Hindi
Day 2: Sit with Saurabh for 60 minutes — understand the compliance audit framework and reporting cadence

Sign-off criteria
Can run a complete hygiene audit independently
Can communicate effectively with housekeeping team
Has run at least one debrief in the appropriate tone
Understands Saurabh's audit framework
Arshpreet + Saurabh confirm readiness

Final  ·  Founder Session and Deployment
Once Streams 1 and 2 are complete, the final session is with the Founder, Manisha, and Saurabh together. Half day.

Topics covered
The brand: what GLEUHR stands for, what it does not
The 5-year vision and the role of regions
Non-negotiables — what gets a Regional Head fired regardless of revenue
Founder's expectations from Regional Heads — said directly
'Known Gaps' section of the KRA document — filled in collaboratively at this session
Open Q&A from the Regional Head

Sign-off and deployment
Manisha collects sign-off from every Sales-stream trainer
Saurabh collects sign-off from every Operations-stream trainer
Master Sign-Off sheet shows green across all modules
Manisha + Saurabh + Founder meet the Regional Head together
Known Gaps section of the KRA filled in and signed by all parties
Deployment to the region
